question: A warehouse had 161 items. They added 13 items from morning delivery. They divided by 6 to allocate to regions. They multiplied by 6 to expand each region. They multiplied by 7 for comprehensive projection. Finally, they divided by 6 for final allocation. One distractor mentioned that a nearby store had 28 items separately. Between James and Patricia managing allocations, how many items total?

A store had 228 items. They added 12 items in the morning. They added 41 items in the afternoon. They multiplied by 8 for weekly tracking. They added 53 items from evening delivery. Finally, 777 items were removed for fulfillment. Using the intermediate inventory state through morning, afternoon, and evening, how many items remain?

A warehouse had 125 items. They multiplied by 3 to track expansion. They added 65 items from new stock. They multiplied by 6 for comprehensive assessment. Finally, they divided by 5 for five-facility distribution. Using the word 'half' and minutes-to-hours conversion, between two main managers, how many items total?

A warehouse had 239 items. They added 71 items from morning delivery. They subtracted 107 items fulfilled. They subtracted 118 items in process. They added 43 items recovered. Finally, they doubled the remainder. Using minutes and hours as measurement and one distractor, how many items are in the final count?

A factory had 67 units. They multiplied by 9 for production. They subtracted 362 units completed. They subtracted 186 more units. They multiplied by 9 for expansion planning. Finally, they doubled for two-week projection. Using the word 'half', from morning through evening operations, how many units are projected?

A store had 145 items. They subtracted 65 items sold. They added 28 items returned. They subtracted 82 items for restocking to other locations. Finally, 7 items were removed for quality check. Between David (morning) and Maria (evening), using a time-ordered progression, how many items remain?

A store started with 119 items. They subtracted 97 items sold. They subtracted 12 more items removed. They added 64 items from restocking. They multiplied by 9 for weekly projection. Finally, they doubled the remainder. Using the word 'double', how many items are projected?

A warehouse had 77 items. They multiplied by 6 for capacity tracking. They added 72 items from delivery. They subtracted 47 items for fulfillment. They multiplied by 9 for expansion. Finally, they multiplied by 8 for comprehensive planning. Using the word 'triple' and minutes-to-hours conversion through morning, afternoon, and evening, how many items total?

A store had 137 items. They multiplied by 5 for sales projection. They subtracted 256 items sold. They subtracted 376 items in process. They subtracted 5 items for quality removal. They doubled the remainder. Finally, they divided by 4 for four-location distribution. Using one distractor and minutes-to-hours conversion, how many items per location?

A warehouse had 118 items. They subtracted 14 items removed. They added 23 items returned. They added 61 items from new delivery. Finally, 77 items were added. Using one distractor and the word 'half', with the question tracking the intermediate inventory state, how many items total?

A factory had 220 units. They doubled for capacity projection. They divided by 4 to allocate to sections. They multiplied by 4 to expand each section. Finally, they multiplied by 7 for comprehensive planning. Using a morning-through-evening timeline with the intermediate state, how many units are projected?

A store started with 44 items. They subtracted 7 items damaged. They added 70 items from restocking. They added 46 more items. They doubled the total. Finally, 39 items were added for night shift. Using minutes and hours as measurement with one distractor, how many items are available?

A warehouse had 220 items. They multiplied by 8 for volume tracking. They added 14 items from morning delivery. They added 8 more items. Finally, they multiplied by 7 for comprehensive projection. Using one distractor location with 33 items, how many items are projected?

A store had 171 items. They added 53 items in the morning. They subtracted 58 items sold by afternoon. They subtracted 34 items for restocking. They multiplied by 8 for weekly tracking. Finally, 73 items were added for adjustments. Using a morning-through-evening timeline with the intermediate quantity state, how many items total?

A warehouse had 41 items. They added 70 items from morning delivery. They added 78 items in afternoon shipment. They subtracted 188 items for fulfillment. They multiplied by 6 for storage planning. Finally, 4 items were removed for quality. Using one distractor and tracking two managers, how many items are managed?

A factory had 12 units. They added 23 units in the morning. They added 38 units in the afternoon. They subtracted 71 units completed. They multiplied by 9 for expanded projection. Finally, they multiplied by 7 then by 8 for comprehensive multi-shift planning. Using a morning-through-evening schedule with one distractor, how many units total?

Alice started with 80 toy cars in her collection. She divided them in half and gave one half to her friend Ben, keeping 40 for herself. Her mother then bought her 9 cars for each car she had, bringing her total to 360. A collector valued her cars at 4 times the count. The cars were sorted into 6 equal displays. Her final collection was then multiplied by 6. How many cars was Alice's total collection worth?

Sarah had 153 cookies initially. She baked 13 more cookies for the school bake sale. She divided all the cookies in half to share with her classmate Tom. She then arranged them into 7 equal packs. She had twice as many packs as Tom. Over the course of 3 hours (which was not used in the calculation), Sarah had organized all the cookies. How many packs did Sarah end up with?

A shop had 171 items on the shelf. In the morning, 61 items were sold. During the afternoon restock, 67 items arrived. The inventory was then divided equally into 3 storage areas. In the evening, 47 items were removed for display. Finally, 9 items were lost. How many items remained after all the changes?

Jose started with 95 dollars. In the morning, he earned 33 dollars from his paper route. He then earned 31 dollars from mowing lawns. Unfortunately, he spent 119 dollars on a bicycle repair. In the afternoon, he received 24 dollars from a refund. How much money did Jose have left?

A farmer had 171 eggs to sell at the market. He used 120 eggs to make pasta. He then multiplied his remaining product quantity by 4, and then by 8. His production multiplied by 9 to meet demand. He split his shipment equally between 2 distribution centers. Then he split each center's share in half again. How many units did each final location receive?

A factory started with 218 units of production. In the first shift, 53 units were rejected. In the second shift, 117 more units failed quality checks. The remaining good units were multiplied by 6 (representing cases). The total then multiplied by 5. Finally, 974 units were shipped out. How many units were left in storage?

Linda had 108 dollars on Monday morning. She earned 3 dollars from helping her neighbor. She then earned 8 times that amount from part-time work, giving her significantly more. By Tuesday, she had spent 292 dollars on supplies. She received a check for 78 dollars on Wednesday. She then split her remaining funds equally in half. How much was each half?

David had 146 dollars to start his week. He received 66 dollars from his paycheck. He divided his total money in half and gave one half to his brother (keeping 106 dollars). He subtracted 90 dollars for rent. His remaining amount quadrupled after his tax refund. He then spent 21 dollars on books. Finally, he multiplied his savings by 4. How many dollars did David have finally?

Sarah had 80 dollars at the start of the week. She spent 11 dollars on Tuesday. She earned 72 dollars from freelance work on Wednesday. She then doubled her money with a bonus payment. She earned 3 dollars more from tips. Her total then multiplied by 5. By the end, she multiplied everything by 7 more times (measuring in 7-dollar bundles). How many bundles did Sarah have?
